outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making a poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or facing the performance impacts of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
With cloud computing, organizations can use only the capacity they need and automatically scale in and out. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation occurs when the demands placed on a workload exceed its capacity, which is a common cause of failure in on-premises workloads. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
Cloud environments allow monitoring of demand and workload utilization, along with automated scaling of resources to prevent over- or under-provisioning. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a cloud service that offers a consistent process to review and measure your architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The service is provided by AWS to review workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
Recommendations are provided by the AWS WA Tool to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps review approaches prior to development, as well as the state of workloads before and during production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does secure key management include for protecting data at rest?
outcomes.answer: Secure key management involves the storage, rotation, access control, and monitoring of the key material needed to protect data at rest for a workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 399]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
Workloads should be designed so that changes are frequent, small, and reversible. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Combining automated deployment techniques with smaller, incremental changes minimizes blast radius and enables faster reversal if failures happen. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Organizations should evaluate both the benefits and risks of deploying changes to workloads while ensuring compliance with governance. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]
Processes must be established to handle both successful and unsuccessful changes to workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]
Teams can use pre-mortems to anticipate potential failures and establish procedures for unsuccessful changes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]
Workload changes should be managed using a mechanism that supports business value delivery and mitigates associated risks. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 135]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS features integrated DNS-based service discovery that creates and manages a registry of service names via the Route 53 Auto Naming API. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
For Kubernetes-managed services, unified service discovery can be enabled through the External DNS project, an incubator project to which AWS contributed. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map provides a service registry for resources like IPs, URLs, and ARNs, offering an API-based service discovery mechanism with faster change propagation and attribute filtering. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Third-party software like HashiCorp Consul, etcd, or Netflix Eureka can also be used for service discovery, supported by an AWS Quick Start for Consul. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Service meshes provide an additional layer for handling interservice communication, enabling tasks like service discovery to be handled entirely within that layer. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS App Mesh can be utilized in service-oriented architectures to offer reliable discovery and access of services. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 65]

outcomes.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
outcomes.answer:
Twelve-factor processes are stateless and share-nothing. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]
Any data that requires persistence must be stored in a stateful backing service, which is typically a database. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Cloud waste happens when incorrectly-sized resources are created or when observed usage patterns differ from what was expected. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
To reduce waste, organizations should follow AWS best practices or seek assistance from their account team and partner to optimize and save costs. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Organizations should periodically generate reports containing AWS Cost Explorer recommendations for Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and Amazon EC2 rightsizing to decrease costs from steady-state workloads, idle, and underutilized resources. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
The ability to attribute resource costs to workloads, individual organizations, or product owners fosters efficient usage behavior and aids in reducing waste. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 37]

outcomes.question: What are the four disaster recovery strategies described for workloads on AWS?
outcomes.answer:
Disaster recovery strategies available within AWS can be broadly categorized into four approaches. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 18]
The four disaster recovery strategies discussed are backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, and multi-site active/active. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
